verdict: Not at fern level (mean 5.3). Compared with the 08d3bff renders, only two things changed (mean pixel difference 1.2-2.0 levels): the kit fabric fix, which makes the jacket and skirt read properly dark against the stone skin, and the suitcase side cover, which shows in wide and window. The stage code has not changed since 26 November, so none of the round-3 stage fixes landed: the charging post still blocks Dawn in wide, the bun still reads as a backwards cap, the aircraft is still toy-like, the sky dashes are still there, the carpet is still smooth vinyl and the window mullion still lands on her head. In seated, the side ladder and chrome zip pulls are still on the case, the shoes are still embossed slipper-boots, and the clasped hands push through each other.

fixes.problem: The suitcase is not unmarked in the frame where it is largest. The four bright horizontal bars on the left sidewall (about x 650-665, y 413-435) are still there. They measure 85-111 graded against a shell of about 30, the same as before the 03:15 cover. The two zip pulls on top (about x 700-745, y 372-385) and the front-pocket zip pull (about x 715-725, y 395-420) are bright chrome. Together they read as a badge and bright hardware. Wide and window are now clean.
fixes.fix: In departure_gate.suitcase(), after props.load, walk every material on the returned object(s). Between the base-colour Image Texture and the BSDF, insert a Map Range (or RGB Curves) that clamps baked values: input 0.0-1.0 maps to 0.0-0.07 linear, so nothing on the case rises above the shell. Set Metallic 0 and Roughness at least 0.6 on every slot, so the zip pulls stop throwing chrome highlights. If the kit cover is a separate mesh, check whether it lands on the opposite sidewall at turn 96 deg. Either extend it to both sidewalls, or add a stage-side nylon patch: a beveled box about 0.012 x 0.075 x 0.07 m, parented to the case on the sidewall over the ladder, with the shell material. Re-render seated and zoom in 3x on x 630-800, y 300-600 to confirm.

fixes.problem: The shoes (people.dawn()'s shoes04) still read as grey rubber slipper-boots with a dark sock band, not plain black flats. They measure 52-69 graded, lighter than the charcoal case (31) and the jacket (18). The left toe still carries an embossed stamp that reads as a brand mark (visible in the raw at x 480-500, y 590-600). The emblem rule applies, and the stage docstring promises black flats.
fixes.fix: Kit change (Codex owns people.py): in people.dawn(), replace shoes04 with a plain low-cut shoe (shoes01, shoes02 or shoes06, whichever has no emboss) tinted BLACK_SHOE. Until then, do it in the stage: get the f"{h.name}_shoes04" object. In each of its materials, set the Normal Map or Bump strength to 0 (this removes the stamp), base colour about (0.025, 0.024, 0.024), Roughness 0.5 and Specular IOR Level 0.3. That brings the shoes under the case's value. Check that the sock band then reads as part of the shoe, not as a separate dark sock.

fixes.problem: charge_post_c, at (-2.45, 0.45), still stands between the camera and Dawn's suitcase (image x 487-525, y 400-580) and overlaps the case. charge_post_b, at (3.95, 0.45), is a second plain grey slab at image x 1140-1175. Both read as untextured grey slabs, not furniture.
fixes.fix: In departure_gate_set.dressing(), delete charge_post_c, or move it to (-9.3, -0.6) against the column at (-9.6, -1.0). Move charge_post_b against the column at (4.4, 5.3), at (4.1, 5.05), or delete it. If one stays in shot, give it the dark brushed material (base value about 0.06, roughness 0.45, anisotropic 0.5), not the mid steel.

fixes.problem: The lighting does not isolate Dawn. The pool from the key fitting lands mostly on the empty carpet behind her seat. That aisle (image x 560-700, y 420-520) measures 117, and the apron floor beyond the glass behind her measures 113. Her back is a dark 44, so only her pale head reads. The aircraft (72-108) and the podium display (135) also compete. The far right wall crushes to 5, and 14% of the graded frame sits at 6 or below.
fixes.fix: For the wide only: move the pool spot (fx_-0.6_+3.1_pool) to (-0.7, 3.15, H-0.03), toward the glass, and narrow spot_size from 36 to 28 deg, so the disc's back edge stops at her seat back instead of spreading over the aisle. Set TRIMS['wide'][RIM] to 1.2, so dawn_rim gives her shoulders and the back of her head an edge. Add 'mast_light_*' trims of 0.5 for the wide, and 'jb_lamp_*' trims of 0.6, so the apron and the nose drop about one stop below her head. Bring pod_disp_screen and pod_mon_screen emission from 2.6 down to about 1.0 for this camera. Target: her head and shoulders are the brightest thing within 2 m of her, and the carpet 2 m behind her is at least 1.5 stops darker than her pool.

fixes.problem: From behind, Dawn's bun still reads as a backwards baseball cap: a smooth dome with a protruding peak at the back. In seated, the ribbed hair reads as a knit beanie. The stage's lowering (scale 0.95/0.78/0.9, z -0.022) is too small to read.
fixes.fix: In departure_gate.dawn(), take the bun much further. Scale about its centroid by (0.8, 0.55, 0.7), and offset it by (0, -0.012, -0.06) toward the nape, so it sits as a low chignon tucked against the top of the neck and does not stick out from the crown. Then look at the window and wide renders and check that no horizontal edge protrudes behind the skull. If the hair material has a ridge bump or normal map, halve its strength so the hair reads as sculpted, not knitted.

fixes.problem: The clasped hands interpenetrate. The left hand's fingers lie flat and splayed and pass into the right hand, and the right thumb stands straight up like a stub (image x 410-490, y 325-370). It reads as a clump of fingers, not hands at rest.
fixes.fix: In lap_hands(), stop the hands crossing. Rest the right hand palm-down on the right thigh, then lay the left hand over the right wrist, not through the fingers: reduce the inward angle on hand_fk from 40 to about 22. Bring UPPER['fingers'] down to an 18-25 deg curl, with the thumbs tucked alongside the index finger. Re-run the hand-gap solve so both palms sit 5-10 mm above the skirt, then check from the seated camera at 3x.

fixes.problem: The aircraft reads instantly and carries no livery, but it is toy-like. The cockpit panes are oversized for the nose, and hard specular hot-spots make the nose look plastic. About 12 bright cabin windows are bunched at the front and read like a barcode. In wide, the nose gear is hidden by the sill and the bridge-to-door join is unclear.
fixes.fix: Fuselage paint: Roughness 0.45-0.5, Specular IOR Level 0.3, Coat 0, base value about 0.35. Scale the flight-deck pane outlines in flight_deck() by about 0.75 about their sill centre. Cabin windows: run them along the whole visible fuselage at 0.53 m pitch, emission 0.25-0.35 (from the current near-white), with about 30% of them unlit at random so they read as windows. Lower the wide camera's aim by about 0.1 m, or raise its z by about 0.3 m, until the nose-gear wheels clear the sill. Or accept the gear as hidden and make sure the bellows visibly meet the L1 door in the window frame.

fixes.problem: The vertical mullion at image x about 770 runs straight down onto the crown of Dawn's head: a tangent. The floodlit nose, the brightest value in the frame, sits right beside her head.
fixes.fix: Move the window camera from (-2.05, -1.35, 1.5) to about (-2.35, -1.35, 1.5), keeping the aim, so her head sits inside one pane against the darker jet-bridge ribs. Add 'mast_light_*' trims of 0.6 for this camera, so the nose drops about 0.7 stop below her head and shoulder edge. Give her an edge light for this camera only: an area light of 0.3 x 0.3 m, about 25 W, cool, above and in front of her toward the glass, at about (SEAT x, ROW_Y + 0.9, 2.4), aimed back at her head, so the silhouette separates.

fixes.problem: White dashes float in the sky and the upper glass (most visible in window, y 20-130). They are reflections of the dimmed ceiling lenses and read as artefacts, not as a reflected room.
fixes.fix: In departure_gate_set.fixture(), for every lens at level DIM or BACK_FX level, set the lens object's visible_glossy = False, or lower the DIM lens emission from 1.3 to about 0.35. Keep the key fitting's lens glossy-visible, so one coherent reflection of Dawn's light stays in the glass. Optionally lower the window glass refl from 0.075 to 0.05.

fixes.problem: The key is a pure top light. Dawn's face (63) is darker than her shins (83) and the empty seat at frame left (89). The bottom right fifth of the frame is an empty mid-grey floor slab. At 45 mm the back rows are only mildly soft.
fixes.fix: Set the seated lens from 45 to about 70 mm. Back the camera off along its line to keep her feet and the case whole, with the frame bottom about 0.2 m below her shoes. Keep f/1.8 and focus on fx_dawn. Add a soft cool fill for her face: an area light of 0.5 x 0.5 m, about 15 W, at about 1.2 m from her face, 30 deg to camera right, at eye height, so the face lifts by about half a stop and the shins stay below it. Extend flag_near_seats about 0.4 m so the near empty seat drops at least 1 stop under her.

fixes.problem: The carpet reads as smooth vinyl tiles: no fibre, no pile, no seams visible at frame scale.
fixes.fix: In departure_gate_mats.carpet(), add a Noise texture (scale 700, detail 2) into Bump at strength 0.12, plus a Wave texture (bands, scale about 120) whose direction rotates 90 deg on alternate 0.5 m tiles, for pile direction. Draw seams at 2 mm, about 10% darker. Keep tile value variation within plus or minus 3%. Set Roughness 0.95 and Specular IOR Level 0.2.

fixes.problem: The podium display is a flat bright patch (135) with no visible spill. The white panel high on the far wall (x 975-1065, y 62-95) reads as a blank lightbox. The right wall and the ceiling crush to 0-8, so the room loses its edge.
fixes.fix: Set screen_front emission to about 1.0 for the wide, and raise pod_disp_light and pod_mon_light from 4-5 W to about 8 W, so the spill shows on the desk and the queue. Halve the high wall panel's emission. Add a wall-washer for the right wall: an area light of 3.0 x 0.2 m, about 20 W, cool, 0.3 m off the wall at 3.0 m height, pointed down. That holds the wall at about 10% grey after the grade, instead of 2%.
